nodes.title: Compile-time rejection of 16 injected handler bugs: axum-like shape 1/16, capability-typed shape 13/16 (rustc 1.88, std-only)
nodes.summary: Own experiment: two ~125/105-LOC std-only Rust SDK+handler stubs, 16 single-edit mutants from the map's bug classes, cargo check per mutant, oracle run for those that compile. Shape A (plain axum-like: pub-field Principal with Default, clonable Db, ambient send_email/http_get, String HTML): 1 rejected (M14 use-after-commit, E0382 from ownership), 15 compiled and oracle-confirmed buggy (M11 structural). Shape B (private-field non-Default Principal, tenant-scoped non-Clone TenantDb<'r>/TenantCache<'r>, effect-class Ctx<'r,Read|Write|Net>, typestate Tx<Open>->Committed gating send_email, Html built only by escape/raw_static, validated Url, Secret w/o Display, Granted<Cap> proof for delete): 13 rejected, 1 compiled-but-neutralized (M3 cross-tenant cache key: SDK namespaces keys, bug not expressible), 2 compiled-violation (M15 same-tenant ownership, M16 archived visibility: semantic). Rejection codes: E0599 x5 (absent API), E0308 x3, E0382 x2, E0277, E0425, E0423, E0521.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Toy SDK authored by us with knowledge of the mutants (selection bias toward B); mutants single-edit, not LLM-generated; 5 of 13 rejects are absent-API (E0599), i.e. API minimalism, not type cleverness; no runtime/async, no real axum; n=16 only.
nodes.underclaim_risk: 13/16 vs 1/16 is deterministic, reproducible from results.json; semantic classes (ownership, visibility) remain unprotected by any shape, which is the honest residual - would be covered by Cedar/oracle tests, not types.
nodes.specifics: files: /home/patrickd/aegis/research/state/raw/round-003/08-exp/shape_a, shape_b, run_mutants.py, results.json; rustc 1.88.0 cargo 1.88.0; target/ deleted

nodes.title: Rejection diagnostics for agent repair: B rejects average 18.5 lines / 950 chars (10-34), A's only reject 21 lines; in-crate privacy errors suggest 'make the field public' (cross-crate removes it)
nodes.summary: From the same run: 13 B rejects: stderr lines mean 18.5 (min 10 M10, max 34 M11 lifetime escape), chars mean 950; single primary error each except M11 (3 errors, E0521 'borrowed data escapes outside of function' - most opaque). Absent-API rejects (E0599 'no method named all_notes found for struct TenantDb') name the missing capability directly = good repair signal and direct evidence the capability is absent. Hazard: E0423/E0616-type privacy errors inside the same crate print 'help: consider making the field publicly accessible' and 'its field is private, but it's local to this crate and its privacy can be changed' - an agent obeying the compiler would weaken the boundary. Verified fix: moving sdk to a separate path-dep crate (x2/) yields the same error without the help line. Also: all rejects are first-compile; no model-run repair rate measured (no API spend).
nodes.overclaim_risk: Message length is a weak proxy for repairability; no agent was run; rustc 1.88 formatting may differ in newer versions.
nodes.underclaim_risk: The privacy-help hazard is a concrete, cheap-to-fix agent-safety finding; underclaiming it risks the SDK being weakened by the very agents it constrains.
nodes.specifics: L5: sdk must be a separate crate with CODEOWNERS/lint (deny edits to sdk/** by agent sessions); app crate #![forbid(unsafe_code)]

nodes.title: Claw-SWE-Bench (2606.12344, v2 2026-09-29): in an agent harness Rust is the best language for 7 of 11 models; Go the worst for all 11
nodes.summary: 350 instances, 8 language groups, 43 per language, OpenClaw harness, 11 models. Rust resolved rate: GPT 5.5 93.0, Claude Opus 4.7 88.4, MiMo-v2.6-flash 81.4, GLM 5.1 81.4, DeepSeek-V4 Pro 79.1, Kimi K2.6 74.4, Seed 2.0-mini 55.8; Python for same: 78.0, 82.0, 70.0, 70.0, 68.0, 66.0, 54.0. Go worst everywhere (33.3-64.3). Parsed from the PDF table F.2 locally. No contamination analysis located in text.
nodes.overclaim_risk: n=43 per language -> binomial 95% CI about +-12-15pp; one harness; language effects confounded with repo difficulty/test quality; no contamination analysis; benchmark authors' own curation.
nodes.underclaim_risk: Direction (Rust >= Python/TS in an agentic compile-test loop for frontier models) is consistent with SWE-bench Multilingual (Rust highest of 7) so not just noise from one source.
nodes.specifics: Rust vs Python: Opus 4.7 88.4 vs 82.0; GPT5.5 93.0 vs 78.0; TS: Opus 81.4, GPT5.5 79.1

nodes.title: SWE-bench Multilingual (SWE-agent + Claude 3.7 Sonnet, 300 tasks): Rust 58.1% (25/43), Go 31.0%, C/C++ 28.6%, overall 42.7%
nodes.summary: Official page: Rust 25/43 58.14, Java 23/43 53.49, PHP 21/43 48.84, Ruby 19/44 43.18, JS/TS 15/43 34.88, Go 13/42 30.95, C/C++ 12/42 28.57; overall 128/300. 2025-era model; only one model on the page. Repo-level: nushell 100%, tokio 55.6%.
nodes.overclaim_risk: n=43 per language; one agent/model (2025); repos in public GitHub = contamination possible; difficulty not matched across languages.
nodes.underclaim_risk: Rust being top in both this and Claw-SWE-Bench from independent construction suggests Rust is not an agent handicap in repo-level loops.

nodes.title: FPEval/PROBE exact numbers: one-shot gap Haskell 18.8pp / OCaml 9.0pp below Java for GPT-5; PROBE Rust gap is 3pp (GPT-4.1-mini) to 13pp (Qwen2.5 14b)
nodes.summary: FPEval (2601.02060, FPBench 721 tasks) pass@1 GPT-5: Haskell 42.34, OCaml 52.16, Scala 58.36, Java 61.14; GPT-4o 27.18/36.20/38.83/43.69; GPT-3.5 14.15/9.43/19.28/22.19. GPT-5 compile-error share Haskell 24.28%, OCaml 13.73, Scala 9.27, Java 4.62. Self-repair (GPT-5 correct of 721): Haskell 287->301, OCaml 376->396, Scala 420->431 (+2-5pp; prior node had no repair numbers). Contamination: only GPT-4o checked, Java 52.0->32.8 and Scala 35.8->21.6 after cutoff (suggests inflated Java baseline), Haskell/OCaml flat; paper has internal text/table inconsistencies. PROBE (2607.13820, CodeNet 1651 problems, 2025-era models): pass rate Python vs Rust: GPT-4.1-mini .70/.67, Gemini-2.0-flash .57/.55, Qwen2.5-Coder14b .44/.34, DeepSeek-Coder-v2 .41/.31, Qwen2.5-14b .38/.24, Qwen2.5-Coder7b .36/.25. Rust last with most compile failures; gap shrinks with model strength.
nodes.overclaim_risk: One-shot, no agent loop; Java contamination makes the 'gap to Java' an overestimate; PROBE models are old/small.
nodes.underclaim_risk: Prior node's 'Rust hardest' is true but magnitude is 3pp at frontier-ish scale: do not read it as a Rust penalty.

nodes.title: Compiler-feedback evidence 2025-26: type-constrained decoding >50% fewer compile errors; RustAssistant ~74% fix; generative compilation 20.7%->13.1% non-compiling; FPEval repair +2-5pp; agents bypass checks (9x any, unsafe)
nodes.summary: (a) 2504.09246 (Apr-May 2025): type-constrained decoding, >50% fewer compile errors, HumanEval/MBPP + TS. (b) RustAssistant 2308.05177 (ICSE 2025): peak ~74% on real-world Rust compile errors. (c) Generative Compilation 2607.13921 (Jul 2026): 7 models, repo-level Rust translation (CRUST-bench) + API update: non-compiling outputs 20.7% -> 13.1% vs post-generation feedback; functional correctness 59.5 -> 63.0 (+3.5pp); Lean-mechanized calculus. (d) FPEval RQ3: one repair round adds only +2-5pp for GPT-5. (e) Counter-evidence: agentic TS PRs use 9x more `any` (2602.17955) though accepted 1.8x more; AdaTrans 2606.31706 reports LLMs resort to unsafe/raw pointers to silence borrow checker; monorepo case 2607.13080: model switch dominates language. (f) 2606.08444: Rust crate hallucination rates consistent across models; compiler does not stop invented dependency names. Net: compile feedback helps modestly (+3-6pp functional, ~35% fewer non-compiling) and agents will game it where the type system has an escape hatch -> the boundary must be enforced by forbid(unsafe_code)/no-any-equivalent lint and SDK-crate separation.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Several are abstract-level reads only (no per-model tables); different tasks/metrics are juxtaposed; no controlled typed-vs-untyped agent ablation exists in what I found (confirmed gap).
nodes.underclaim_risk: The absence of a controlled ablation is itself a finding: claims 'strict types help agents' rest on indirect evidence; the local mutant experiment is the only direct (compile-time) measurement.

nodes.title: Opt-in guards (axum extractors, Rocket request guards, Convex getUserIdentity, Leptos server fns) fail by omission; mandatory-by-construction context (Encore access level, Cloudflare bindings, shape B Ctx) does not
nodes.summary: axum 0.8.9 docs: extractors are handler parameters; an handler that lacks the extractor is simply unchecked; docs' own AuthenticatedUser example has placeholder 'actually perform the authorization'. Rocket 0.5 guide claims access violations 'guaranteed prevented at compile-time' but only if the guard type is not otherwise constructible, and a handler that omits the guard is unchecked. Leptos book: server functions are 'syntax sugar for a public API', no auth mechanism in that chapter. Convex: ctx.auth.getUserIdentity() returns null; handler must check. Contrast: Encore //encore:api requires an access level token (public|auth|private) in every endpoint annotation and static analysis builds schemas; Cloudflare Workers: capability granted only by declared binding, 'a permission and an API in one piece'. Experiment: shape B makes authenticated Principal and tenant-scoped handles non-optional fields of a Ctx the router constructs, so missing-authn is unrepresentable while missing-authz (Granted<Cap>) is a type error only for operations that demand the proof.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Doc pages read through a summarizer; absence statements ('docs don't say') are weak; did not run each framework.
nodes.underclaim_risk: Rocket's guard-as-proof is closer to shape B than axum's; it is a pattern, not a default.

nodes.title: Handler-SDK design space vs bug classes (independent enumeration): which shapes make authn/tenant/effect/HTML/SQL classes unrepresentable
nodes.summary: Candidates and what they make unrepresentable (evidence = docs read + experiment): (1) axum-style extractors: nothing by default (A: 1/16). (2) Rocket guards: authn if guard private-ctor; omission unchecked. (3) Leptos/Dioxus server fns: RPC ergonomics, public endpoint, authz manual. (4) Ur/Web (prior node hist-urweb-*): SQL/XSS statically; UrFlow checks SQL-written policies over all paths; authz policy still app-specific; niche (bus factor). (5) Servant (Haskell, type-level API; docs URL 404 on fetch - unverified here). (6) OCaml Dream: handler = request->response function, middleware = handler->handler; features sessions/CSRF helpers as functions, not types. (7) Gleam Wisp 2.2.2: handler takes app Context, middleware via `use`; no typed authz. (8) Encore: mandatory access level + generated typed clients (Go; compile-time analyzer). (9) Convex: validators + manual identity check. (10) WIT/wasi-http: capability = imported interface; wasi-http repo archived 2025-11-25 and merged into WebAssembly/WASI (phase 3, 0.3 draft). (11) Cloudflare binding model. (12) Shape B: Rust newtype/typestate capabilities; 13/16. Only (8),(11),(10),(12) make an unauthenticated or un-granted effect inexpressible by *construction* rather than convention. HTML/SQL class: only typed-HTML/typed-query builders (Ur/Web, shape B) remove it; string-taking APIs do not.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Servant/IHP/Dream/Wisp security claims unverified at primary-doc depth (Servant page 404, IHP search returned nothing); matrix partly inferred.
nodes.underclaim_risk: WIT's capability-import model could give B's guarantees language-independently; not tested here.

nodes.title: Drop-an-artifact deploy prior art: Spin OCI push + cosign verify (digest-pinned); Shuttle shut down (Pro stopped 2026-01-16); Fly launch; Cloudflare bindings
nodes.summary: Spin v3 docs: `spin registry push ghcr.io/<user>/<app>:<ver>`, `spin up -f <ref>`, tags mutable so pin `@sha256:`, Cosign 2.0+ sign/verify supported. Fermyon vendor claim ~0.5 ms cold start (no independent per-request benchmark found). Shuttle (git-push-deploy Rust PaaS): docs state shutdown, Pro projects stopped 2026-01-16, community accounts deleted early 2026, repo archived (mirror claim) - sustainability warning for single-vendor DX platforms. Fly speedrun: `fly launch` reads Django/Rails/Phoenix/Node projects; no measured time. Dioxus 0.7 subsecond hot-patch experimental (dx serve --hotpatch), no axum recipe.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Vendor claims unmeasured; Shuttle successor Neptune only from search snippet.
nodes.underclaim_risk: A signed OCI-style artifact with digest pin already exists as precedent (Spin) so 'signed artifact drop' is not novel; novelty would be the verifier-gated handler ABI.

nodes.title: Local loop lower bound: std-only SDK+handlers cold debug build 0.33-0.40 s (159 MB RSS), warm cargo check 0.11 s; axum build not measurable offline
nodes.summary: rustc 1.88.0, heavy.sh (6 GB cap, nice 15), shape_b 105 LOC: cold debug build 0.40/0.33 s, peak RSS ~159 MB; incremental cargo check after touch 0.11 s. axum/tokio/hyper not fully present in offline registry (hyper 1.9/1.12, tokio 1.45/1.52 cached; no axum) so axum cold/incremental check is an implementation-phase spike: protocol = fresh crate with axum 0.8.9 pinned, `heavy.sh cargo check` cold and after touching one handler, 3 runs, record wall/RSS; decision it informs: whether per-mutant compile-fail CI (30+ checks) is affordable.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Tiny std-only crate; says nothing about axum/tokio dependency tree compile cost which dominates real loops.
nodes.underclaim_risk: Even so, the SDK-surface check itself is sub-second, so a 'compile-fail corpus' CI gate costs little if deps are compiled once.

nodes.title: Cloudflare Workers bindings = capability grant ('permission and an API in one piece'); runtime isolation incidents remain (workerd URLPattern OOB cross-tenant secret read, Check Point 2026)
nodes.summary: Binding model: resources reachable only via env bindings declared in config; secrets never exposed to code. Caveat from docs: isolates may be reused when only bindings change, so construct clients from env per request not in global scope. Separately, search results report a workerd cross-request global-state leak fix (July 2026, details not found) and Check Point's URLPattern out-of-bounds read letting one Worker read another tenant's secrets (self-hosted users told to update to workerd v1.20260619.1) - not verified at primary source here. Implication: API-level capability does not replace isolation; both layers needed.
nodes.overclaim_risk: CVE/incident parts come from a search summary; primary release note not located.

nodes.title: CANDIDATE DECISION: first-party handlers = native Rust against a separate-crate capability-typed SDK (shape B) + compile-fail mutant corpus as CI gate; alternatives listed with reversal conditions
nodes.summary: Chosen (provisional): Ctx<'r, E: Effect> built only by the router (Principal non-optional, no Default, private fields), TenantDb/TenantCache lifetimes bound to request and non-Clone, Tx<Open>->Committed gating effects, Html/Url/Secret newtypes, Granted<Cap> proofs; sdk in its own crate; app crate forbid(unsafe_code); no raw-SQL or raw-HTML API. Acceptance criterion: `cargo test` runs a corpus of >=30 compile-fail mutants (trybuild-style or the run_mutants.py harness) and requires >=90% of structural-class mutants rejected, with the semantic classes (ownership, visibility) delegated to Cedar policy + differential oracle tests; error-message guard: no rejected mutant's diagnostic may contain 'make the field public'-type help (test greps stderr). Alternatives: (a) plain axum + lint/clippy rules (A: 1/16; reverse if LLM runs show equal defect rate); (b) WIT component handlers with capability imports (language-independent, adds Wasm TCB, wasi-http repo archived/merged Nov 2025 - reverse if Wasm host chosen for third-party code); (c) Ur/Web or other typed-web language (rejected: bus factor 1, no release since 2020 per map); (d) Encore/Convex-style mandatory annotation + codegen (needs codegen TCB); (e) RLS-only (map: fails when agents create tables). Reversal conditions: LLM agent trials show B raises repair-loop iterations > 2x with no defect drop; or async lifetime ergonomics make B handlers fail to compile in realistic axum/tokio integration (spike).
nodes.overclaim_risk: Based on toy SDK + indirect literature; no LLM trial; async/tokio integration (lifetimes in async fn, Send bounds) untested and may break the non-'static handle design.
nodes.underclaim_risk: Cost of the decision is low (SDK is ~100 LOC of types) and it is falsifiable cheaply, so even moderate evidence justifies prototyping.
nodes.specifics: Spike S1 (impl phase): same 16 mutants against real axum 0.8.9 + tokio handlers, async fn, with B-style extractors (FromRequestParts producing Principal; handle with request lifetime via extension), measure rejected/compiled. Spike S2: paid LLM trial 20 tasks x 2 shapes counting iterations-to-green and mutant rate.
